title: The Invention Lab Handbook
subtitle: Foundations you can reason with. Projects you can start.

chapters.title: Work like an inventor
chapters.summary: Turn an idea into a question, a prototype and a defensible next decision.

chapters.title: Math and physics at the workbench
chapters.summary: Use units, proportions, vectors, energy and simple models to predict behavior.

chapters.title: Measure, experiment and debug
chapters.summary: Separate repeatability, bias and real change; design a test that answers one question.

chapters.title: Design for people and purpose
chapters.summary: Translate observations into requirements, compare concepts and test useful prototypes.

chapters.title: CAD that survives the next change
chapters.summary: Build design intent with constraints, datums, components and dimensioned interfaces.

chapters.title: Materials and manufacturing choices
chapters.summary: Match stiffness, environment, process and repair needs to a material and manufacturing route.

chapters.title: 3D printing as a manufacturing process
chapters.summary: Reason from toolpaths, orientation and fit experiments to a usable printed part.

chapters.title: CAM and the shared machine shop
chapters.summary: Understand stock, workholding, coordinate systems and toolpaths before machine operation.

chapters.title: Forces, structures and failure
chapters.summary: Trace loads, distinguish strength from stiffness and challenge a simple structural model.

chapters.title: Mechanisms, motors and motion
chapters.summary: Choose the motion first, then reason about speed, torque, transmission and support.

chapters.title: Circuits you can explain
chapters.summary: Build a mental model of voltage, current, resistance, power and circuit measurements.

chapters.title: Sensors, signals and power
chapters.summary: Connect real sensors to real supplies while accounting for loading, sampling and noise.

chapters.title: Microcontrollers and embedded behavior
chapters.summary: Make small devices respond predictably with timing, state machines and explicit failure states.

chapters.title: From circuits to PCBs and chips
chapters.summary: Connect semiconductor and digital-logic concepts to schematic, layout and fabrication decisions.

chapters.title: Software, data and reproducible work
chapters.summary: Use code, logs, version control and tests to make engineering experiments repeatable.

chapters.title: Feedback and control
chapters.summary: Understand what a controller observes, changes and cannot fix; test it in simulation first.

chapters.title: Robotics as a system
chapters.summary: Bring coordinates, mechanics, sensing, actuation and software into one testable machine.

chapters.title: AI and computer vision for makers
chapters.summary: Compare a learned model with a simpler baseline, evaluate failures and bound its authority.

chapters.title: Connected devices that remain understandable
chapters.summary: Choose interfaces, define messages and keep a useful local system when networks fail.

chapters.title: From guided build to independent project
chapters.summary: Plan an integrated build, manage interfaces and evidence, then hand it to someone else.

paths.title: Build your foundation
paths.result: A project brief, a measurement notebook and a small reproducible experiment.

paths.title: Design and fabricate a useful object
paths.result: A measured bracket or mechanism, with a drawing, fit evidence and revision record.

paths.title: Make a sensing device
paths.result: A low-voltage sensor/logger with a schematic, state machine and readable data.

paths.title: Build a small intelligent system
paths.result: A simulated positioning or sensing system, with a plan for an optional bounded bench prototype.
